As of 130 AM Tuesday... 

1) A return to below normal temperatures and gusty winds today 
behind a cold front. 

A surface cold front continues to move through central NC at the 
moment. It will continue to push south and west today, reaching the 
panhandle of FL by tonight. Continental Polar high pressure over the 
Midwest and Great Lakes today will strengthen and shift into the NE 
US tonight, setting up a developing cold air damming situation for 
Wednesday. A tight pressure gradient will be in place today and 
tonight, with NE winds gusting to 20-25 mph, infrequent to 30 mph 
across the Coastal Plain. These gusts should diminish this evening, 
though some infrequent gusts to 18 mph are possible overnight.

It will be much cooler today, with highs around 5 degrees below 
normal in the mid to upper 50s. Near-freezing temperatures are 
possible across the NW Piedmont early Wednesday, though mid/high 
clouds and boundary layer stirring may limit radiational cooling. 
Elsewhere, lows in the mid to upper 30s will be common. 

KEY MESSAGE 2... A potent storm system will affect much of the 
eastern United States including our region beginning Wednesday and 
lasting into Thanksgiving Day. Chilly temperatures in the upper 
30s and 40s, gusty NE wind to 35 mph, and heavy rain of 1 to 3 
inches can be expected Wednesday afternoon into Thanksgiving morning.

The only notable changes in the past 6-12 hours with the observations
and guidance have been for some of the models to be a bit quicker in 
developing the rain on Wednesday morning, especially over southern 
sections. If so, rain would then more quickly move into the I-40 
corridor of central NC through the afternoon. However, other 
model solutions including the EC and many ensembles suggest that the 
dry air ridge will win out much of Wednesday, holding the heaviest 
rainfall off until late day. We are leaning toward making little 
change to previous forecasts at the current time.

Other small trends include the models tracking the low pressure a 
bit more toward the coast and shift it northward into VA more 
quickly Thursday. Thus, the rain may end a bit quicker on 
Thanksgiving day with some brightening later in the day. We are 
leaning in that direction.

The dry air ridge (DAR) is still expected to be strong (1040+ mb) as 
it builds down the eastern seaboard through the western Carolinas 
and GA today through 12z/Wed. Strong dry and cool air advection will 
lead to dew points crashing into the 20s west and 30s east tonight. 
As the mid/upper trough approaches later tonight, some continued 
cutting off of a portion of the mid/upper level trough over the Gulf 
Coast occurs behind the lead vorticity maximum that will be 
approaching our region late tonight. Low pressure initially develops 
with the first feature out in Gulf Stream off Fl, then rides north
along the developing trough extending up the Carolina coast. As this 
occurs, rain spreads into the southern sections fairly quickly 
Wednesday morning, and the rest of region through the afternoon. 

In addition, gusty NE winds may become strong enough to down some 
tree limbs with gusts to 35-40 mph Wed. into Wed. evening as 
the pressure gradient tightens. These windy conditions will 
combine with the progressively wetter and colder conditions during 
Wednesday afternoon and evening. CAD will quickly develop and 
temperatures will likely be hard pressed to rise much more than the 
lower to mid 40s in the Piedmont and lower to mid 50s in the Coastal 
Plain. After collaboration with surrounding offices, we lowered 
temperatures considerably from the NBM on Wednesday and keep them 
steady or slowly rise Wednesday night. 

As the system continues to evolve, it appears that the rain will be 
most widespread late Wednesday through early Thursday morning as the 
main low pressure lifts northward, possibly as far west as the I-95 
corridor by 12z/Thu. The widespread rain would taper to areas of 
light rain, fog and mist through early afternoon as the main lift 
moves into VA. Storm total rainfall amounts of 1 to locally 3+ 
inches still appear likely, again mostly focused on Wednesday 
afternoon through 12z-15Z Thursday. Then later Thursday, the track 
of the mid/upper low should keep additional rainfall east of the 
mountains limited to scattered light showers into Thanksgiving night 
with developing downslope flow behind the system.

Steady temperatures in the 40-45 range may come up a little by 
12z/Thu in the Piedmont damming region. Readings in the Coastal 
Plain may rise into the upper 50s and lower 60s as the low pressure 
tracks nearby. 

Surface winds will decrease Thursday under the lower pressures, then 
pick up again (in downslope westerly fashion) late Thursday, 
Thursday night, into Friday morning. Highs in the 50s and 60s NW to 
SE expected. 

Partly sunny and breezy weather is expected Friday with the NW winds
